html:
The Shoshone, who call themselves Newe, are an Indigenous people of the western United States, from the Great Basin to the northern Rockies. They speak a Numic language of the Uto-Aztecan family.

There were four main divisions:

  • Eastern Shoshone in Wyoming
  • Northern Shoshone in southern Idaho
  • Western Shoshone in Nevada, eastern California and Utah
  • the Goshute of western Utah

In the dry Great Basin they lived in small family groups, gathering seeds and pinyon nuts. Further north and east they took up horses in the late 1600s, among the first on the northern Plains, and hunted bison until the Blackfoot, armed with guns, pushed them back. The Comanche split off from them around 1700.

Sacagawea, a Lemhi Shoshone, guided the Lewis and Clark Expedition through her homeland in 1805. Today Shoshone tribes often share reservations with the Northern Paiute or the Bannock.
